newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT - DUTCH CHARTISTS REMAIN UPBEAT ON AEX.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - DUTCH CHARTISTS REMAIN UPBEAT ON AEX.

text.p: Dutch technical analysts remain
bullish with their outlooks for the AEX index this week as it
pushes into new all-time highs.
All four of this week's contributors to a Reuters poll
maintained their forecast of the index in an uptrendd.
The AEX index ended at 631.06 points on Friday, 15.59 points
above the previous Friday. In the week before that the index had
gained 6.59 points. On Monday, the AEX gained 0.81 points to a
new intra-day record of 631.87.

Note - Contributors' own analysis follows.
ABN AMRO - After reaching successfully for several
intermediate targets we set in the past, the AEX has now broken
our target of 630. After consolidating for a day and a day of
panic during which the AEX drifted down 11 points, the Bulls
have picked up their relentless rally in search of record
territory.
Actually nothing has changed since our last comment in which
we wrote: "In our view the Bull market is still in effect, and
the top hasn't been reached yet."
We have no signs of a serious near term correction. In fact,
our advice is to buy on the few dips that might take place
within a day's time frame. Our up focus is being supported by a
target calculation that shows us possible prices of around 650.
Summarising, we state that the LONG side is still the way to
play this market. However, maintain close exit-stop to be
safeguarded from deterioration of profits due to volatile
swings. Buy on the dips.
FIBONACCI PRESS - The intermediate term trend is still up.
The short term trend did manage to stay firm last week, and
reached the expected higher resistance levels around 632. The
market is now at a critical juncture, as the present "once in a
decade blowoff phase" could further accelerate to the upside, or
show a mild correction for a week or two. A drop below 627 will
be the first sign of this correction, and a drop below 623 is a
clear indication (support zone 609/603). Only an immediate rise
above 636 indicates that further acceleration is in force, with
first resistance at 640 and then 654. Critical support for the
bullish case remains at 594.
